UK Recruitment Agency Insolvency Statistics

Latest detailed figures for England and Wales

There were 105 insolvencies among permanent-placement recruitment agencies in England and Wales between January and May 2026, compared with 149 in the same period of 2025. The rolling 12-month total was 301, down from 327 for the previous 12 months.

This covers recruitment agencies placing candidates into permanent roles (the official industry code is SIC group 781). Temporary and agency staffing businesses are recorded separately (SIC group 782).

Comparison

Are recruitment agency insolvencies falling in 2026?

Insolvencies among permanent-placement recruitment agencies were broadly falling in the January to May 2026 period, with 105 cases compared with 149 during the same months of 2025, a fall of 29.5%. That contrasts with administrative and support services overall, where insolvencies fell 21.7% over the same period.

Permanent-placement recruitment agencies accounted for 12.5% of all administrative and support services company insolvencies in the January to May 2026 period (105 of 843 cases), down from 13.8% over the same months of 2025.

Trend

Recruitment agency insolvencies by month

May 2026 recorded 21 insolvencies, against 19 in April 2026 and 43 in May 2025. One month does not establish a trend, but the year-to-date and rolling 12-month totals above are the steadier read; this chart is the detail behind them.

Recruitment agencies sit within the wider company insolvencies by sector data, alongside administrative and support services generally. See also temporary staffing agency insolvency statistics and the UK company insolvency statistics.

Context

Why permanent-placement recruitment agencies are under pressure

General sector conditions, not a claim about any individual company. Read alongside the figures above, not as their explanation.

Direct exposure to hiring confidence

Placement fee income depends entirely on clients actively hiring, so it falls away almost immediately when clients freeze recruitment, with little notice and no way to recover the lost pipeline.

Thin working capital buffers

Agencies are typically light on fixed assets and cash between placements, so a run of quiet months can exhaust reserves faster than in sectors with more physical assets to fall back on.

Practitioner view

What we see in recruitment agency insolvency cases

In the cases we see, recruitment agencies scale their cost base, particularly consultant headcount, to match a hiring boom, then are exposed when client hiring slows and fee income drops away almost immediately.

Placement fee income is inherently lumpy. An agency with a handful of large clients can see a material share of its pipeline disappear when just one of them pauses hiring.

Annual

Recruitment agency insolvencies by year, 2016 to 2025

Recruitment agencies insolvencies rose from 139 in 2016 to a peak of 345 in 2025. The 2025 total of 345 remained well above the pre-pandemic total of 149 in 2019.

Recorded insolvencies reached their series low of 127 in 2018.

How to read this

How to interpret the recruitment agency figures

Recruitment agency insolvencies can move sharply on a small number of cases, since it is a mid-sized sector. Prefer the year-to-date or 12-month rolling total for the steadier read.

The count is a volume, not a failure rate. It is not adjusted for how many agencies are registered, so it cannot be read as a sector-wide risk of insolvency.

This is permanent-placement recruitment only (SIC 781). Temporary staffing agencies sit under a separate SIC code and are covered on their own page.

Method

UK company insolvency statistics: methodology

Company insolvency data is sourced mainly from Companies House. Compulsory liquidation data for England and Wales comes from the Insolvency Service, and compulsory liquidation data for Northern Ireland comes from the Department for the Economy in Northern Ireland.

The headline England and Wales figures use seasonally adjusted data where the Insolvency Service has identified seasonality. Scotland and Northern Ireland figures are shown on an unadjusted basis.

The statistics count formal company insolvency procedures. They do not include members' voluntary liquidations, dissolutions or ordinary company closures.

Data limitations

  • The latest month is provisional and can be revised.
  • Table 1c industry totals by three-digit SIC are published monthly, through the latest headline month; the breakdown by insolvency procedure within each industry is published quarterly.
  • Industry is based on self-reported SIC codes.
  • Registered office addresses are not a reliable guide to where a company traded.
  • Solvent company closures are not included.
